title: Economic connectedness in US Facebook friendship networks is associated with substantially greater local innovation
source_unit: US patenting ZIP Codes, Facebook friendship networks, economic connectedness, patents, breakthrough patents, relocation, and local social shocks
geography: United States; patenting ZIP Codes and Facebook friendship networks

observations.period: Working paper issued September 2026; contemporary Facebook friendship and US patenting geography evidence

denominator.unit: US patenting ZIP Codes and ZIP Codes with breakthrough patents; exact ZIP and user counts not disclosed in the NBER abstract

economic_connectedness.unit: share of high-income friendships in a local Facebook friendship network

patents_per_capita.unit: percent more patents per capita associated with a one-standard-deviation increase in economic connectedness among patenting ZIP Codes

breakthrough_patents_per_capita.unit: percent more breakthrough patents per capita associated with a one-standard-deviation increase among ZIP Codes with breakthrough patents

causal_support.unit: reverse-causality tests, within-inventor relocation, and a fracking-driven shock to non-local friends support a causal interpretation

financing_channel.unit: mechanism tests are consistent with a financing channel linking social capital to innovation

observations.method: The paper links Facebook friendship-network measures to patenting geography, uses reverse-causality tests and within-inventor relocation, and exploits fracking-driven economic shocks to non-local friends as a quasi-experiment.
observations.uncertainty: The NBER abstract does not disclose user or ZIP counts, effect intervals, exact Facebook observation window, patent definitions, or all privacy and exclusion assumptions. Economic connectedness is not the same as trust, local institutions, finance received, firm survival, worker outcomes, or broad social cohesion.
observations.subgroup: US patenting ZIP Codes and ZIP Codes with breakthrough patents; effects are framed around high-income friendship exposure and inventor relocation.
observations.counterinterpretation: Network composition, migration, selection into Facebook, local industry, education, capital markets, and patenting may jointly shape the association; the quasi-experimental results support a mechanism but do not imply every community can reproduce the same effect through social mixing alone.

related_sources.claim: Earlier NBER social-capital evidence finds economic connectedness is among the strongest area-level predictors of upward income mobility; a counterfactual placing low-SES children in counties with the connectedness of the average high-SES child implies about 20 percent higher adult income.
US multinational tax-planning structures concentrate foreign profits and create modeled revenue/activity tradeoffs.
AI-skilled employment and organization capital are associated with recent firm productivity growth.
American Indian economic, educational, and health outcomes vary substantially by place, resources, and historical policy experience.

boundary: This record adds a network and financing mechanism to the US innovation program. It does not establish that friendship exposure alone creates patents, measure privacy or social costs, or connect innovation to local jobs, wages, consumer welfare, or durable place capacity in the same unit.
